topics.label: Process Model
topics.desc: An OS abstraction bundling an address space, open file descriptors, and execution state, isolating programs as independently scheduled units.

topics.label: Threads
topics.desc: Lightweight execution streams sharing a process address space, enabling concurrency with cheaper creation and switching than full processes.

topics.label: Process Lifecycle
topics.desc: States and transitions (new, ready, running, blocked, terminated) a process moves through, driven by scheduling and I/O events.

topics.label: Fork & Exec
topics.desc: Unix pattern where fork duplicates a process and exec replaces its image, the canonical mechanism for spawning new programs.

topics.label: User vs Kernel Mode
topics.desc: Hardware privilege separation where untrusted user code traps into the kernel for protected operations, the foundation of OS isolation.

topics.label: System Calls
topics.desc: The controlled interface by which user programs request kernel services like I/O, process creation, and memory, crossing the privilege boundary.

topics.label: Interrupts & Traps
topics.desc: Hardware and software signals that divert the CPU into kernel handlers, the mechanism underlying I/O, timers, and system calls.

topics.label: Context Switch
topics.desc: Saving one task's CPU state and loading another's, the core scheduling mechanism whose cost bounds practical time-slice granularity.

topics.label: Scheduler Goals & Metrics
topics.desc: Throughput, latency, fairness, and CPU utilization objectives that scheduling policies trade off, often in direct tension.

topics.label: Preemptive Scheduling
topics.desc: Forcibly suspending a running task on a timer or higher-priority arrival, ensuring responsiveness and preventing CPU monopolization.

topics.label: Scheduling Algorithms
topics.desc: Policies like FCFS, SJF, round-robin, and priority that choose the next runnable task, each optimizing different metrics.

topics.label: Real-Time Scheduling
topics.desc: Deadline-driven policies like rate-monotonic and EDF guaranteeing tasks complete within timing bounds for control and media systems.

topics.label: Priority Inversion
topics.desc: A high-priority task blocked by a low-priority lock holder, mitigated by priority inheritance or ceiling protocols.

topics.label: Multiprocessor Scheduling
topics.desc: Distributing runnable tasks across cores with load balancing and affinity to preserve cache locality and avoid contention.

topics.label: Virtual Memory
topics.desc: Per-process address spaces decoupled from physical RAM, providing isolation, overcommit, and a uniform addressing abstraction.

topics.label: Paging
topics.desc: Dividing memory into fixed-size pages mapped via page tables, eliminating external fragmentation and enabling demand loading.

topics.label: Page Tables & TLB
topics.desc: Multi-level translation structures and a cache of recent mappings whose miss and flush behavior dominates virtual-memory performance.

topics.label: Demand Paging
topics.desc: Loading pages lazily on first access via page faults, reducing startup cost and footprint at the price of fault latency.

topics.label: Page Replacement
topics.desc: Algorithms like LRU, clock, and second-chance choosing which page to evict under memory pressure, balancing hit rate against overhead.

topics.label: Thrashing & Working Set
topics.desc: Pathological state where excessive paging starves progress, controlled by tracking each process's working set of active pages.

topics.label: Memory Allocators
topics.desc: Heap managers like buddy, slab, and malloc carving free memory into objects while limiting fragmentation and synchronization cost.

topics.label: Memory-Mapped Files
topics.desc: Mapping file contents directly into an address space so paging serves I/O, enabling zero-copy access and shared memory.

topics.label: Mutex
topics.desc: A mutual-exclusion lock granting one thread at a time exclusive access to a critical section, the workhorse synchronization primitive.

topics.label: Semaphore
topics.desc: A counting synchronization primitive coordinating access to a pool of resources via atomic wait and signal operations.

topics.label: Condition Variables
topics.desc: Primitives letting threads sleep until a predicate holds, paired with a lock to coordinate state changes without busy-waiting.

topics.label: Atomic Operations
topics.desc: Indivisible hardware instructions like compare-and-swap that underpin lock-free algorithms and the implementation of all higher locks.

topics.label: Spinlocks
topics.desc: Locks that busy-wait instead of sleeping, optimal for very short critical sections where context-switch cost exceeds spin time.

topics.label: Reader-Writer Locks
topics.desc: Locks permitting concurrent readers but exclusive writers, boosting throughput on read-heavy shared data at fairness risk.

topics.label: Memory Ordering & Fences
topics.desc: Hardware reordering of loads and stores requiring fences and acquire/release semantics to make concurrent code correct.

topics.label: Race Conditions
topics.desc: Bugs where outcome depends on unsynchronized interleaving of accesses to shared state, the root cause of most concurrency defects.

topics.label: Critical Section Problem
topics.desc: The requirement to enforce mutual exclusion, progress, and bounded waiting around shared-resource access, the core sync challenge.

topics.label: Deadlock
topics.desc: Circular waiting where threads each hold resources the others need, halting all involved, characterized by four Coffman conditions.

topics.label: Deadlock Prevention & Avoidance
topics.desc: Strategies breaking Coffman conditions or using safe-state checks like the Banker's algorithm to keep systems deadlock-free.

topics.label: Livelock & Starvation
topics.desc: Failure modes where threads stay active yet make no progress, or are perpetually denied resources by unfair scheduling.

topics.label: Classic Sync Problems
topics.desc: Canonical exercises like dining philosophers, producer-consumer, and readers-writers that expose deadlock and fairness pitfalls.

topics.label: False Sharing
topics.desc: Performance bug where independent variables on one cache line force coherence traffic, silently serializing parallel threads.

topics.label: Shared Memory IPC
topics.desc: Mapping a common memory region into multiple processes for the fastest IPC, requiring explicit synchronization to stay correct.

topics.label: Pipes & FIFOs
topics.desc: Unidirectional byte-stream channels connecting processes, the backbone of shell pipelines and simple producer-consumer flows.

topics.label: Message Queues
topics.desc: Kernel-managed queues delivering discrete, ordered messages between processes with optional priorities and bounded buffering.

topics.label: Unix Domain Sockets
topics.desc: Local bidirectional channels using the socket API, supporting datagrams, streams, and passing file descriptors between processes.

topics.label: Signals
topics.desc: Asynchronous software interrupts notifying processes of events, constrained to async-signal-safe handlers and easily mishandled.

topics.label: Futexes & Eventfd
topics.desc: Low-level kernel primitives enabling fast userspace locks and lightweight cross-process wakeups with minimal syscall overhead.

topics.label: File Abstraction
topics.desc: The uniform file-and-descriptor model letting programs treat disks, pipes, and devices through one read/write/seek interface.

topics.label: Inodes & Metadata
topics.desc: Per-file structures holding size, permissions, timestamps, and block pointers, decoupling file identity from directory names.

topics.label: Virtual File System
topics.desc: A kernel abstraction layer presenting many filesystem types through one API, enabling mounts and pluggable backends.

topics.label: Journaling & Crash Consistency
topics.desc: Write-ahead logging of metadata so a filesystem can recover to a consistent state after a crash without full scans.

topics.label: Page Cache & Buffering
topics.desc: In-RAM caching of file blocks that absorbs reads and batches writes, the dominant factor in real-world I/O throughput.

topics.label: Disk & I/O Scheduling
topics.desc: Reordering and merging block requests to optimize seek patterns and latency, increasingly tuned for SSDs over spinning disks.

topics.label: Concurrency vs Parallelism
topics.desc: The distinction between structuring overlapping tasks and physically executing them simultaneously on multiple cores.

topics.label: Blocking vs Non-Blocking I/O
topics.desc: Whether an I/O call suspends the caller or returns immediately, the central tradeoff shaping server concurrency architecture.

topics.label: Event Loop & Reactor
topics.desc: Single-threaded model multiplexing many connections via readiness notification, driving Node.js, Nginx, and async runtimes.

topics.label: I/O Multiplexing
topics.desc: Readiness APIs like epoll, kqueue, and io_uring that let one thread monitor thousands of descriptors scalably.

topics.label: Async/Await & Coroutines
topics.desc: Language constructs that suspend and resume functions without OS threads, expressing async logic in sequential-looking code.

topics.label: Thread Pools
topics.desc: Pre-spawned worker sets pulling tasks from a queue, amortizing thread creation cost and bounding concurrency under load.

topics.label: Green Threads & Fibers
topics.desc: User-space scheduled lightweight threads multiplexed onto OS threads, scaling to millions of tasks with tiny stacks.

topics.label: Actor & CSP Models
topics.desc: Concurrency paradigms replacing shared state with message-passing between isolated entities, avoiding locks by design.
